fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Kimora Lee Simmons and Tim Leissner’s Custody Battle Takes a Stunning Turn. * Kimora Lee Simmons has requested that her estranged husband, Tim Leissner, receive primary custody of their 11-year-old son, Wolfe, in their divorce proceedings. * This request is in contrast to Leissner's original filing, where he asked for joint legal and physical custody and spousal support. * The couple's legal dispute also involves major disagreements over money, with Simmons asking the court to block Leissner from collecting spousal support and requesting support for herself. **Kimora Lee Simmons** has taken an unexpected position in her divorce from **Tim Leissner**. ## A surprising court filing has shifted the focus of Kimora Lee Simmons and Tim Leissner's legal dispute. However, she rejected Leissner's custody proposal and instead asked the court to grant him primary legal and physical custody of Wolfe. Simmons asked the court to block Leissner from collecting spousal support. She also requested spousal support for herself and asked that he pay her legal fees.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Trump administration admits grants for clean energy were canceled based on politics - The Washington Post
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: The Trump administration has again acknowledged in court documents that it terminated $7.6 billion in grants for hundreds of clean energy projects “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state,” in this case, 16 states that voted for Democrat Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. WASHINGTON — The Trump administration has acknowledged in court documents that it canceled $7.6 billion in grants for hundreds of clean energy projects “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state” — in this case, 16 states that voted for Democrat Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. “This administration has now admitted in court what has long been obvious: it terminated nearly 300 cost-cutting energy projects for no reason other than the fact that the states they were in did not vote for the president in the 2024 election,” said Rep. Marcy Kaptur of Ohio and Sen. Patty Murray of Washington state.
